design_context_from_root.target: Tentative NHANES2007–08 comparison, not accessed by curator
design_context_from_root.status: Design metadata supplied by root, not source evidence and not a target population distribution.

reported: See source manifest and 51 evidence items. All numeric evidence items are reported values; no derived coefficients or pooled moments are supplied.

unknown.item: Joint distribution of age, sex, BMI and serum urate in the quota target, including within-cell covariances, tails and nonlinearities.
Exact source summaries in each target age/sex quota cell. No selected source reports all eight cells.
A US-specific descriptive anchor for ages55–64 in these selected locators. Bogalusa stops at54, CHS starts at65; Korea supplies a broad age context with different population selection.
Age-conditional BMI distributions and urate residual distributions within sex. Marginal means/SDs do not establish Gaussian, lognormal or any other family.

An urate-on-BMI regression with age and sex covariates, residual variance and coefficient uncertainty. Bogalusa Table2 reports the opposite outcome direction, and its standardized beta is not a raw correlation.
Race composition or race-specific mixing weights for the quota target. Bogalusa source proportions do not establish target weights.
Menopause, renal function, treatment use, alcohol/diet, comorbidity and their joint distributions with requested variables in the target.
How to transport older CHS statistics pooled across ages≥65 to ages65–79 only, or Korean open-ended age summaries to bounded US quota cells.
Sampling uncertainty for most descriptive means/SDs and regression coefficients. Reported SDs are not SEs; no uncertainty was invented from p-value thresholds.

transport_issues: Geography, selection, ancestry composition, calendar period, medication exclusions, laboratory assays, missing-data handling and age truncation differ across the three studies.
Quota sampling fixes cell counts but does not provide within-cell age distribution or BMI/urate moments.
Cross-study differences cannot be assigned to age effects alone. No individual-level link between these cohorts exists in this packet.
Source-supported relationships and summaries may conflict after transport; there is no prescribed generator, parameter reconciliation, desired sign or evaluation answer in this packet.
